fuel_vintage_rule.2018-2019: LF2016 FBFM13, pre-event by 2-3 calendar years
fuel_vintage_rule.2023-2024: LF2022 FBFM13, pre-event by 1-2 calendar years; LF2022 fuel disturbance layers include disturbances through 2022
fuel_vintage_rule.terrain: LF2020 elevation, treated as static terrain

limitations: FPA-FOD occurrence points are not verified ignition coordinates and have at least section-scale source precision.
Twenty per year is still a screened western-US large-fire sample, not a representative national benchmark.
All 80 cases have daily gridMET context and an explicit versioned SimFire proxy. This is not an hourly replay or physical validation.
Fuel map vintages are pre-event and public-service available, but are not per-event vegetation surveys.
MTBS IDs support later visual reference only; no historical perimeter defines the simulator reward.
purpose: Small, reproducible, real-incident environmental cohort for SimFire policy experiments; not a physical reconstruction.

source.license_and_citation: USFS Research Data Archive says FPA-FOD may be used without additional permissions or fees; cite Short (2026), DOI 10.2737/RDS-2013-0009.7. Check joined raster and perimeter products separately.
source.name: USFS FPA-FOD current edition

selection_rule.sampling: Stable SHA-256 ranking of FOD_ID, greedily preferring one event per state before filling the annual quota; selection does not rank by final size.

split_rule.note: Out-of-time validation/test. Years 2020-2022 are omitted from this first cohort because their best pre-event FBFM13 layer is not presently available from the public ImageServer endpoint; do not substitute a post-event fuel map.
split_rule.unit: whole incident; events from one fire never cross splits

training_rule: The agent learns only from SimFire rollouts on each case's environmental inputs. FPA final size and MTBS historical perimeters stay hidden from observations and rewards.
